title: deterministic-eni-failover-and-acl-staging-for-controlplane-dns-cutover
author: Maya Lin
description: Motivation: customers running Private control planes reported nondeterministic ENI placement during controlplane upgrades which caused transient routability gaps and DNS flaps. This PR introduces deterministic ENI allocation ordering across AZs, an ACL staging mechanism for safe subnet-level security group transitions, and a staged DNS cutover sequence with TTL ramping and reconciliation hooks. Changes touch Terraform modules, Helm hooks for the installer controller, and upgrade/rollback orchestration scripts. Key goals: 1) eliminate race in ENI attachment ordering so that controlplane instances always get primary ENIs in a predictable AZ order during upgrades; 2) provide an ACL staging workflow that allows temporary permissive ACLs during handoff then tightens back once health checks pass; 3) orchestrate DNS resolver records with TTL lowering and automated rollback on health regressions so customer applications experience controlled switchover. This work is intended to reduce incident windows during upgrades and make rollback deterministic and auditable. The description below is an integrated summary of changes, tests, and rollback plan. Terraform: added `eni_allocator` submodule (eni_allocator/main.tf, variables.tf, outputs.tf) that implements prioritized ENI claim per AZ using a tag-based lease and an opportunistic backoff. The module exposes `preferred_az_sequence` and `claim_retry_policy` and switches ENI attachment to use a lifecycle precondition so allocation ordering is deterministic. Security groups & ACLs: introduced `acl_stage` resource and a `staging_profile` that temporarily opens management ports and peered-controlplane CIDRs during rollout; a controller-backed `acl-stager` Helm hook reconciles and then tightens ACLs. DNS & peering: added conditional route53 private hosted zone record playbook (installer/upgrade/dns_playbook.yaml) that lowers TTL to 30s, creates ambidextrous CNAME targets during traffic mirror, and only flips authoritative records after staged health checks succeed. Also added a peering attach-ordering shim to ensure peering routes are present before ENI promotion. Installer/helm: small Helm chart changes add pre-upgrade and post-upgrade hooks for the ACL stager and a new CRD `ENIAllocator` to surface allocation state for observability. Orchestration: upgrade script (installer/upgrade/orchestrator.sh) runs ENI allocation, ACL staging, DNS TTL ramp, canary traffic test, and automated rollback on failures based on configurable thresholds. Testing: unit tests for Terraform module mocks, integration test harness in perf-canary that simulates AZ loss and validates ENI reselection ordering, e2e with a two-AZ cluster and synthetic liveness probes. Rollback plan: if health fails during any stage, orchestrator triggers: 1) revert DNS authoritative records, 2) demote newly-attached ENIs in reverse order, 3) reapply previous ACL set, 4) tear down temporary peering routes. Migration notes: existing clusters without `ENIAllocator` will continue using the old allocator; the installer supports a staged opt-in via a feature flag `eni_allocator.enabled=true`. Backwards compat: CRD is opt-in and no existing resources are mutated until opt-in, and the staging ACL controller only acts when `acl.staging=true` is present on the ClusterConfig. Related: ENG-1284 (customer upgrade incident), ENG-2410 (rollout automation). Checklist: [x] Terraform module and Helm chart changes implemented and unit-tested [x] Integration test added to perf-canary [x] Upgrade orchestration with explicit rollback paths [x] Documentation updated in installer/README.md [x] Observability: ENIAllocator metrics and events emitted.
